desk.why: Implied is only 1.06x the forecast, below the 1.10x a seller needs. A reason to buy is present (measured event before expiry, realised vol rising above implied) but buying on it has not paid on this desk's history.

facts: NIFTY moved +2.3% over the last 7 sessions and +0.3% on the day, to 25,884.
Gap +54 pts, then the session added +11 pts.
The day closed in the upper half (close - low 151, high - close 90).
ATM IV sits in its 77th percentile of the past year: option premium is rich - selling it pays more, but moves are expected to be bigger.

base.why: No trend worth leaning on (7-session move +2.3%), so the plan sells both sides at the writers' walls, 25,800 and 26,000, and lets time decay work. Note: the desk's volatility rule says stand aside today (Implied is only 1.06x the forecast, below the 1.10x a seller needs. A reason to buy is present (measured event before expiry, realised vol rising above implied) but buying on it has not paid on this desk's history.). This plan overrides it only for the scenario branches; size down.
text: bull put spread: sell 25,500 PE, buy 25,300 PE (credit about 41 pts, Rs 2,679 per lot; max loss Rs 10,321)
bear call spread: sell 26,500 CE, buy 26,700 CE (credit about 38 pts, Rs 2,475 per lot; max loss Rs 10,525)

scenarios.title: Drifts sideways between 25,800 and 26,000
watch: Two daily closes below 26,000 without a new high
Close - open (the body) small, either colour
scenarios.means: The move is pausing. Time decay is working for the seller.
scenarios.action: Hold. Take profit once 50% of the credit is earned.

scenarios.title: Reaches 26,000 and stalls
watch: High - close bigger than close - low (sellers took it back)
26,000 CE open interest still rising (call writers defending)
scenarios.means: Call writers are defending 26,000. A ceiling for now.
scenarios.action: Close today's position (take the profit) and open the new one. It would be about Rs 2,070 in profit per lot here (estimated). Weekly: sell an iron condor, sell 26,000 CE / buy 26,200 CE / sell 25,800 PE / buy 25,600 PE. Call writers are defending 26,000: sell calls at the wall and keep a put spread under the market, so both sides earn while it stalls.

scenarios.title: Breaks out above 26,000
watch: 26,000 CE open interest falling (writers buying back - short covering)
Close near the day's high again
scenarios.means: The ceiling gave way. Next magnets: 26,300 then 26,500.
scenarios.action: Close today's position (take the profit) and open the new one. It would be about Rs 1,618 in profit per lot here (estimated). Weekly: or buy a spread, buy 26,200 CE / sell 26,600 CE. Momentum version: a bull call spread toward 26,600. Costs premium; loses it if the breakout fails. If it spikes past 26,300 in one session with VIX rising, take profit instead of chasing.
scenarios.odds: Reached 26,300 in 42.5% and 26,500 in 25.6% of past cases (normal 47.3% / 32.2%).

scenarios.title: Falls to 25,800 and holds
watch: 25,800 PE open interest still rising (put writers defending)
scenarios.action: If it holds: keep today's position, or add nothing (weekly). If it breaks: close today's position and switch to sell 25,800 CE / buy 26,000 CE (weekly). Exact strikes for every expiry are in the position matrix.
scenarios.odds: Dipped to 25,800 in 71.1% of past cases (normal 67.6%).

scenarios.title: Breaks down below 25,800
watch: 25,800 PE open interest falling (put writers exiting)
scenarios.means: The floor gave way. Next: 25,500 then 25,300.
scenarios.action: Close today's position. It would be about Rs 832 in profit per lot here (estimated). Weekly: sell a spread, sell 25,800 CE / buy 26,000 CE. The old floor 25,800 becomes the ceiling: sell calls at it. Or buy a spread: buy 25,600 PE / sell 25,200 PE.
scenarios.odds: Dipped to 25,500 in 44.3% of past cases (normal 42.1%).

rules: Take profit on any spread once 50% of its credit is earned; the rest is not worth the risk.
Close any spread once its loss reaches 1.5x the credit taken, whatever day that is. Holding into expiry is fine; size smaller on expiry day.
Act on daily closes, not intraday spikes. The OI checks use the next morning's bhavcopy.
Credits for rolls and add-ons are set by prices on the day you act; today's numbers are a guide only.
limits: None of the desk's positioning signals (PCR, max pain, OI flow, walls) has passed its own backtest for this horizon, so the history study is the main evidence.
